edits.old: template <class T> struct plain<const T> : plain<T> {};

name: plain-strips-only-one-level
why: the specializations do not repeat: const int& becomes const int.

edits.new: template <class T> struct plain<T&> { using type = T; };

edits.old: template <class T> struct plain<const T> : plain<T> {};
edits.new:
template <class T> struct plain<const T> : plain<T> {};
template <class T> struct plain<T*> : plain<T> {};

name: is-container-needs-only-value-type
why: begin() and end() are not checked.

name: is-container-v-does-not-look-through-references
why: the const and reference are not stripped.

name: element-type-of-an-array-is-missing
why: C arrays have no element type.

edits.old: template <class T, std::size_t N> struct element_type<T[N]> { using type = T; };
template <class T> struct element_type<T, std::enable_if_t<is_container<T>::value>> { using type = typename T::value_type; };

name: element-type-has-a-type-for-everything
why: the primary template defines type = T: element_type<int> is int.

edits.old: template <class T, class = void> struct element_type {};
edits.new: template <class T, class = void> struct element_type { using type = T; };

name: call-result-decays

name: first-value-returns-a-reference
why: decltype(auto) instead of auto: a reference into the container.

name: first-ref-returns-a-const-reference
why: const auto& instead of decltype(auto): not assignable.

name: call-through-is-always-noexcept
why: noexcept even when the function may throw.

name: copy-all-always-uses-memcpy
why: non-trivial types are copied byte by byte, without their copy assignment.

name: copy-all-copies-one-too-many
why: the loop runs to n inclusive.

edits.old: for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) to[i] = from[i];
edits.new: for (std::size_t i = 0; i <= n; ++i) to[i] = from[i];

name: copy-all-reverses-the-order
why: the elements land in reverse order.

edits.old: for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) to[i] = from[i];
edits.new: for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) to[n - 1 - i] = from[i];
